title: TEA-Bench-BR: Can Coding Agents Turn a Branching Clinical Specification into Correct Code?
abstract: arXiv:2611.27895v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Coding agents increasingly implement rules written by domain experts, and bugs in such code are silent: it runs and returns a plausible answer. We introduce TEA-Bench-BR, a benchmark built on the Brazilian pathway for early autism (TEA) screening: three fictitious instruments with the structure of real ones, a multi-professional referral flow, and export to FHIR R4 with the national RNDS profiles, all specified in Portuguese. A generator samples each task's parameters (144 tasks, 6,798 hidden cases), and the hidden cases kill all 1,955 non-equivalent mutants of the reference. With Gemma 4 as the agent, the 12B solves 38.0% of single-instrument tasks and none at the FHIR level; the 31B solves 77.8%, 85.2% and 78.7% at levels 1 to 3 and passes over 99% of the hidden cases, its remaining failures mostly in input validation rather than clinical decisions. With the same tasks in English, the 31B solves 57.4% at level 3, as its code validate

translated_title: TEA-Bench-BR：编码智能体能否将分支化的临床规范转化为正确的代码？
translated_abstract: 编码智能体越来越多地被用于实现由领域专家编写的规则，而这类代码中的缺陷是“静默”的：代码可以运行并返回看似合理的答案。我们提出了TEA-Bench-BR，这是一个基于巴西早期自闭症（TEA）筛查路径构建的基准：包含三个结构仿照真实量表的虚构评估工具、一个多专业转诊流程，以及导出为采用国家RNDS配置文件的FHIR R4格式，全部规范均以葡萄牙语编写。一个生成器对每个任务的参数进行采样（共144个任务、6,798个隐藏测试用例），这些隐藏用例能够杀死参考实现的全部1,955个非等价变异体。以Gemma 4作为编码智能体，12B模型解决了38.0%的单量表任务，而在FHIR层面则无一解决；31B模型在第1至第3级的解决率分别为77.8%、85.2%和78.7%，并通过了超过99%的隐藏用例，其剩余的失败大多出现在输入验证而非临床决策方面。当相同的任务以英语呈现时，31B模型在第3级的解决率降至57.4%，因为其代码验证……（摘要在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了TEA-Bench-BR——一个基于巴西早期自闭症筛查流程、以葡萄牙语规范编写的多层级代码生成基准，用以严格评测编码智能体将分支化临床规范转化为正确代码的能力，结果揭示了大模型在复杂任务层级和输入验证方面的显著局限。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces TEA-Bench-BR, a multi-level benchmark based on Brazil's early autism screening pathway with Portuguese-language specifications, designed to rigorously evaluate coding agents' ability to translate branching clinical specifications into correct code, revealing significant model limitations at complex task levels and in input validation.
